full_judgment:
2. Respondent No. 2 as complainant filed a petition of complaint before the Magistrate, 1st Class, Sonargaon against the accused-appellants alleging, inter alia, that appellant No. 1 is the widow of his brother late Md Shajahan and Appellant No. 2 is the present husband of appellant No. 1. Appellant No. 3 is the father and one Aminul Islam is the brother of appellant No. 1. The complainant's brother Md Shajahan died on 25-3-88 leaving widow appellant No. 1, two minor sons Md Shahriar and Shajahan, mother Pokraj Begum and 5 brothers and 4 sisters as his heirs. Soon after the death of his brother appellant No. 1 re-married appellant No. 2 and are living together as husband and wife by swearing an affidavit dated 18-2-90 at a time when the minor sons of his brother were under the custody of the complainant. Appellant No. 1 suppressing the re-marriage filed OC Suit No. 5 of 1991 before the Upazila Court, Sonargaon impleading an unknown person as a defendant and obtained a decree on 24-7-91 for disposal of the property of the minors by suppressing the truth and practicing fraud upon the Court The Court permitted the transfer and directed appellant No. 1 to deposit the sale money to the bank with a further direction to deposit the cheque book before the Court. After obtaining fraudulently such permission all the accused-appellants together sold the land of the two minor sons by two registered deeds dated 21-11-91 at a price of Taka 2 lac while the real worth of the property is Taka 12 lac. They did not deposit the sale money into the bank in violation of the Court's order and kept these in their custody for misappropriation. Coming to know about the said fact and obtaining thereafter the certified copy of the decree in Title Suit No.5 of 1991 complainant- respondent No. 2 repeatedly requested the appellants not to transfer the minors property to others but they failed to persuade them in the matter. The mother of the complainant who was witness No. 1 in the petition of complaint filed Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 1992 before the Assistant Judge, Sonargaon seeking redress of her grievance on this matter but as the matter relates to criminal offence the complainant and the witnesses were advised to lodge a complaint before a criminal Court. On 3-11-92 the complainant requested Appellant No. 1 to deposit the entire sale money to the bank as per direction of the Court but Appellant No. 1 refused to do so and thereby fraudulently misappropriate the said amount. 

 (1) The learned Judges of the High Court Division without entering into the merit of the case at all wrongly laid down a general proposition of law that before exhausting the remedies provided under section 265C or 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure an application under section 561A of the Code for quashing the proceeding is premature. 

 (2) The civil Court's order having been violated in a proceeding for guardianship Appellant No. 1 is liable to explain her conduct before the civil Court which passed the order and directed her to comply with the same. The civil Court being in seisin of the entire matter the direction given to file the petition of complaint before a criminal Court which has no independent jurisdiction to interpret an order of the civil Court is uncalled for in the facts of the case. 

 (3) The story of re-marriage of accused- appellant No.1 having been disbelieved by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition No. 358 of 1991 on 23-1-92 arising out of a Paribarik Adalat suit for guardianship of the two minor sons of Appellant No.1, the complainant, namely, the uncle of the two minor sons, who lost in the guardianship case, out of a spirit of revenge and vendetta has filed this harassing proceedings which is an abuse of the process of the Court and, as such, the proceeding ought to have been quashed. 

 "In view of the existing legal position as noticed above, we hold that a person accused in a criminal case can only prefer an application under section 561A for quashing the said proceeding if he becomes previously unsuccessful in his application either under section 265C or 241A, otherwise his application under section 561A shall be premature." 

 7. This general observation is not at all correct. Section 265C in Chapter XXIII speaks of discharge of an accused in a trial before Court of sessions. Section 241A in Chapter XX speaks of discharge of an accused in a trial by a magistrate. These are two independent sections of the Code which deal with discharge of an accused brought for trial in respect of cases triable by a Court of sessions and by a Court of magistrate. These two sections indicate that when an accused is brought for trial before a Court of law the Court upon hearing the parties and on consideration of the record of the case and the documents may discharge the accused. These two sections have nothing to do with quashing of a proceeding. Section 561A is an independent inherent power of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court and this power can be exercised in case of abuse of process of Court and for securing the ends of justice and or to give effect to any order under the Code. In none of the decisions given by the Appellate Division or High Court Division the views of the learned Judges of the High Court Division have ever been accepted. This is altogether a new and novel approach. The learned Judge did not care to enter into the merit of the case and without entering into the merit of the case such a general and sweeping observation is unfortunate and ought not to have been made in the facts and circumstances of the present case. Such general observation on the ground of prematurity as has been made by the learned Judges is not sustainable in law. Apart from this, the learned Judges ought to have entered into the merit of the case before refusing to quash the proceeding. 

 8. It appears that Appellant No. 1 is the widow of late Md Shajahan, brother of complainant-respondent No. 2. Appellant No.2, it is alleged, is the present husband of Appellant No. 1 and Appellant No. 3 is the father and one Amirul Islam is the brother of Appellant No. 1. It is on record that in OC Suit No.5 of 1991 of the Upazila Court, Sonargaon Appellant No. 1 became the guardian of her two minor sons. The Court permitted Appellant No. 1 to transfer the property on behalf of the minors and to deposit the sale proceeds to the bank with further direction to deposit the Cheque Book in Court. As per the petition of complaint Appellant No. 1 sold properties by registered kabala on 21-11-91 and did not deposit the money in Court. It may be mentioned that the matter of guardianship came up to the Appellate Division wherein by our judgment dated 23-1-92 in CP No. 358 of 1991 we upheld the guardianship of mother Appellant No. 1 and found that the story of remarriage with appellant No. 2 was not proved. It also appears that the mother of the complainant who was witness No. 1 in the petition of complaint filed a Miscellaneous case being Case No. 16 of 1992 before the Assistant Judge, Sonargaon with regard to the two registered sale deeds dated 21-11-92 wherein it was alleged that accused-appellant No. 1 did not deposit the sale money in the bank in violation of the Court's order and misappropriated the same. The civil Court is in seisin of the matter. The civil Court could very well investigate into the matter with regard to its own order and, as such, the civil Court cannot direct the complainant to file the petition of complaint before a criminal Court. Further, we find that the complainant-respondent No. 2 being the uncle of the two minors of Appellant No. 1 failed to be the guardian of the minors. In order to take revenge the complainant has started this criminal proceeding against a helpless widow by alleging, what has already been decided to be false, that she remarried and by abusing the process of Court Appellant No. 1 and others are being harassed and humiliated. 

 9. It is very surprising that the learned Judges of the High Court Division enunciated a wrong proposition of law without entering into the merit of the case. This is not only illegal but also not a proper exercise of jurisdiction vested in the Court itself.
